paper.title: Ab-Initio Solution of the Many-Electron Schrödinger Equation with Deep Neural Networks
paper.authors: David Pfau, James S. Spencer, Alexander G. de G. Matthews, W. M. C. Foulkes

results.system_description: N2 at bond length 2.068 bohr, all electrons, singlet (7 up, 7 down), clamped nuclei
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the trained FermiNet from a separate MCMC run after optimization (Appendix A); local energies are clipped only in the gradient, not in the energy evaluation.
results.notes: Geometry: bond length 2.068 a0, Table II. The original TensorFlow FermiNet with 16 block-diagonal determinants.

results.system_description: Li atom, all electrons, clamped point nucleus, 2 up and 1 down electrons
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the trained FermiNet from a separate MCMC run after optimization (Appendix A); local energies are clipped only in the gradient, not in the energy evaluation.
results.notes: Ground-state energy of the isolated atom, Table I ('FermiNet' column). N_up = 2, N_down = 1: not printed, but the 2S ground term of Li lies only in this sector (up to the mirror N_up <-> N_down). Pfau et al. assign electrons 'according to the nuclear charge and spin polarization of the ground state of the isolated atom' (Appendix, FermiNet architecture and training). The original TensorFlow FermiNet with 16 block-diagonal determinants.

results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the trained FermiNet from a separate MCMC run after optimization (Appendix A); local energies are clipped only in the gradient, not in the energy evaluation.
results.notes: Geometry: Table X, the G3 geometry (Appendix G). Table X of Pfau et al. labels the coordinates 'Position (a_0)', but they are in angstrom (C-N 1.464, C-H 1.100; in bohr the C-N bond would be 0.77 angstrom), and the instance stores them in angstrom; the energies near CCSD(T)/CBS confirm the angstrom geometry. The original TensorFlow FermiNet with 16 block-diagonal determinants.
